narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Reads the lines that introduce each speech.

job.name: Job
job.note: The afflicted just man of Hus, answering his friends and pleading his cause before God.

2.t: I have often heard such things as these: you are all troublesome comforters.

3.t: Shall windy words have no end? or is it any trouble to thee to speak?

4.t: I also could speak like you: and would God your soul were for my soul.

5.t: I would comfort you also with words, and would wag my head over you.

6.t: I would strengthen you with my mouth, and would move my lips, as sparing you.

7.t: But what shall I do? If I speak, my pain will not rest: and if I hold my peace, it will not depart from me.

8.t: But now my sorrow hath oppressed me, and all my limbs are brought to nothing.

9.t: My wrinkles bear witness against me, and a false speaker riseth up against my face, contradicting me.

10.t: He hath gathered together his fury against me, and threatening me he hath gnashed with his teeth upon me: my enemy hath beheld me with terrible eyes.

11.t: They have opened their mouths upon me, and reproaching me they have struck me on the cheek, they are filled with my pains.

12.t: God hath shut me up with the unjust man, and hath delivered me into the hands of the wicked.

13.t: I that was formerly so wealthy, am all on a sudden broken to pieces: he hath taken me by my neck, he hath broken me, and hath set me up to be his mark.

14.t: He hath compassed me round about with his lances, he hath wounded my loins, he hath not spared, and hath poured out my bowels on the earth,

15.t: He hath torn me with wound upon wound, he hath rushed in upon me like a giant.

16.t: I have sowed sackcloth upon my skin, and have covered my flesh with ashes.

17.t: My face is swollen with weeping, and my eyelids are dim.

18.t: These things have I suffered without the iniquity of my hand, when I offered pure prayers to God.

19.t: O earth, cover not thou my blood, neither let my cry find a hiding place in thee.

20.t: For behold my witness is in heaven, and he that knoweth my conscience is on high.

21.t: My friends are full of words: my eye poureth out tears to God.

22.t: And O that a man might so be judged with God, as the son of man is judged with his companion!

23.t: For behold short years pass away, and I am walking in a path by which I shall not return.
